basis: Independent hand construction: choose synthetic radius R and central angle alpha; arc length is R * alpha. Endpoints (R, 0) and (R*cos(alpha), R*sin(alpha)) give the chord by Euclidean distance. These choices represent geometry only, with no cable properties or qualification claim.
tolerance_basis: For alpha away from zero, relative tolerance 1e-12 allows floating-point rounding after the helper's 200 bisections. Near straight, c/L = 1 - alpha^2/24 + O(alpha^4), so relative radius error is approximately 12 times ratio error divided by alpha^2. At 0.1 degree, binary64 epsilon gives approximately 9e-10; relative tolerance 1e-8 allows rounding in endpoint construction and inversion. Absolute tolerance is zero so the small-radius case cannot pass on an absolute floor.
